answer: A falcon circling above the river valley this morning reminded me of my grandfather, who spent thirty years as a ferryman before the town finally built a bridge. He never resented the crossing; he said the water taught him to read weather the way a sailor reads stars. When the bridge opened, he kept rowing anyway, out of habit, and people still paid him in small coins, one of which he later had set with a pearl for my grandmother. Progress rarely erases what patience built.
